overall: Atlanta is recording an unusually warm overnight baseline of 77°F at 03:00 ET with zero warming velocity, indicating temperatures have plateaued early in the morning rather than cooling. High dewpoints near 73°F signal very humid air, and broken cloud cover at a low ceiling (~427m) with 62% cloud fraction is suppressing any further radiative cooling overnight — and will likely temper daytime solar heating as well.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show meaningful spread: NBM comes in lowest at 80.8°F, ECMWF at 83.7°F, and HRRR most aggressive at 86.2°F — a ~5.4°F range suggesting genuine uncertainty in convective potential. The META (fused) model peaks sharply at the 86-87°F bucket (26.4%), which aligns best with HRRR and slightly above ECMWF; however, the ensemble odd-bucket signal independently flags 81-82°F as Tier 1 high confidence, creating a notable internal tension in the model suite.
max_temp_prediction: The warm 77°F floor at 3 AM with a very moist airmass (dewpoint 73.4°F) supports an above-average high, but persistent broken cloud cover will constrain afternoon solar insolation and limit the day's heating potential. Balancing the META model's 86-87°F modal bucket against the NWP model mean (~83.6°F) and the cloud/humidity drag, today's TMAX most likely lands in the mid-80s — confidence is moderate given the cloud cover uncertainty and spread between models. Best estimate is approximately 85.5°F.
